long_description:
Donkey is the modern trading company. We buy straight from Chinese factories and sell delivered to US importers: one USD price to their dock, duty paid, our own inspectors on the factory floor before the factory gets paid.

We take title, run the inspection, move the money, and offer credit-insured net-45 terms to qualified buyers. The old trading giants ran this coordination with tens of thousands of people. Team in SF and China, English and Mandarin. Know a US importer buying from China? Send them our way: one photo of a part, and we will name their factory. donkey.trade

name: Egoist Machines
long_description:
We're building AI Passport, a personal memory layer that works across AI apps. Every AI product you use today keeps its own memory of you: ChatGPT has one, Claude has one, and every AI-powered app is starting to build one too. None of them talk to each other, you can't see most of what they've stored, and you re-explain yourself to each new tool.

AI Passport replaces those scattered profiles with one card you own. Your preferences, history, and goals live in one place, and new information lands in an inbox where you approve or reject it before it's saved. Apps that want to use your context request a pass, which grants them access to only the categories you allow and can be revoked at any time. Receipts show you exactly which app read what, and when.

For a user, this means any AI app can know you from the first message. 
For a business, personalization works in both directions: a storefront can retrieve a customer's taste, sizes, and budget and personalize instantly instead of running an onboarding quiz, and a support organization can keep one memory of each customer across tickets, teams, and agents, so every new case starts with what the company already knows about the person.

Rex agents run continuously in the background and resolve work to SLA standards so cash keeps moving. We're live with pre-IPO tech companies, managing  >$500m in receivables from F100 companies, cutting manual follow-up cycles from weeks to hours.

We founded Rex after spending four years building Sequence, an a16z-backed finance ops platform, from zero to Series A — where we saw firsthand that at-scale, O2C still runs on manual labour.

Rex is the #1 winner of the Vercel AI Accelerator out of 2,500 teams, selected by Guillermo Rauch and leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Browserbase and more.

long_description:
Prized lets non-engineers build, deploy, and share secure internal tools with AI, no engineering required. You don't need to know where the data lives, what APIs to use, or which connectors you need. Just describe what you want (a customer lookup, a dashboard, an approval flow), and Prized builds the tool on top of the right company data inside a governed boundary.

The people who feel the pain of missing internal tools most are non-engineers. They understand the workflow best but are blocked by the software layer, so they wait on engineering, duct-tape spreadsheets together, or increasingly rip company data into Claude Code and Cursor with no thought to permissions, sharing, or governance.

Prized makes security the default, enforced in the infrastructure rather than left to whoever built the tool. Each tool gets access only to the tables and integrations it was explicitly granted, credentials are workspace-scoped so tools can't cross org boundaries, and outbound calls go through a controlled layer. 

As an employee builds and shares, a teammate forks it and re-points it at their own data, and over time the company builds up a library of governed tools it actually owns.

Hudson was founding engineer at Gander (F24, acquired by Archer), then full-stack at Suno. Marinos studied CS and ME at Stanford and was on the same Gander team.

Deploy a new model only when the held-out eval is beaten. Serve it wherever you want. Production data feeds back into training and compounds performance over time.

Test. Learn. Deploy. Repeat.

long_description:
Geopolitical conflicts and natural disasters frequently expose the vulnerability of the American chemical industry. The reason? Production is centralized and fossil fuel-dependent. The solution? Localized production using an undervalued resource: biogas. The US produces enough biogas to make over $20 bn/y worth of chemicals, but 60% is wasted in low-margin applications or flared altogether.

Rise Reforming is commercializing a modular process to transform this underutilized biogas on-site into cheap, supply-secure chemicals. Our beachhead market is dimethyl ether (DME), used as an aerosol propellant and a low-carbon fuel additive in propane. Our target market is methanol: an established billion $ chemical and the future of low-carbon shipping.

We're doing our pilot project at a Chicagoland wastewater plant. This will be the first wastewater biogas-to-methanol demo in the Americas.

We're hiring for a senior chemical process engineer. Apply here: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rise-reforming/jobs/wJ9Q9nv-senior-chemical-process-engineer

long_description:
Floracene shows independent surgery centers the best-priced equivalent implant for every procedure based on their manufacturer contracts. 

Every orthopedic surgeon we've talked to says the same thing: 90%+ of expensive implants they use are clinically interchangeable, but the choice comes down to habit, brand comfort, or the device rep. US surgery centers spend ~$7B a year on implants, and in orthopedic and spine cases the implant alone runs ~40-60% of the total cost of the procedure. Roughly ~20-30% of that spend is recoverable by switching to a clinically-equivalent device. Instead of defaulting to the implant they trained on, a surgeon sees the 3+ equivalent options side by side and switches to the one that protects the case's margin.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

At a big hospital the surgeon picks the implant but isn't spending their own money, so price doesn't impact the decision. At an independent surgery center the physicians own the economics, so a cheaper equivalent goes straight to their bottom line. They have every incentive to switch. They just don't have the information or the tooling.
one_liner: Optimized medical device purchasing for independent providers

name: GUILD
long_description:
GUILD is making aerospace parts faster and cheaper than today’s defense supply chain. We win defense contracts, automate manufacturing, and deliver to the government's door.

We’ve built an AI-native operating model for defense contracting: a company brain that connects requirements, pricing, supplier capability, compliance, manufacturing, finance, and delivery so each contract makes the next one faster and cheaper.
one_liner: Making aerospace parts faster and cheaper for defense

name: RealPact
long_description:
RealPact builds AI agents that handle the paperwork behind real estate transactions. They find property records like deeds, tax records, permits, parcel data, and MLS information, then use that data to fill out contracts, organize documents, track deadlines, and help brokerages close deals faster.

We are starting by automating transactions and will expand into other parts of brokerage operations. Much of the software used across the real estate industry is outdated. With today’s advances in AI, we can build agents that handle this operational work and create modern software around how brokerages actually work.

We currently sell to brokerages in New Hampshire and are expanding quickly.
one_liner: AI-native OS for Real Estate Brokerages
subindustry: Real Estate and Construction -> Housing and Real Estate

name: Buildbox
long_description: Buildbox helps product teams improve the human-agent experience. We analyze user intent, agent behavior, and outcomes to find where users get stuck or lose trust, then turn those findings into ranked, reproducible issues.
one_liner: Understand how users experience your AI agents

name: Riften
long_description:
Riften builds earned intelligence: models that come out of a company’s own work instead of out of a lab.

One environment variable points an existing application at Riften instead of OpenAI or Anthropic. Riften routes each request to the least expensive model likely to handle it, using open-weight models we host whenever they are sufficient. Customers lower inference costs before any training begins.

Because Riften sits in the request path, real tasks and their outcomes create training evidence the company controls. Riften uses that evidence to improve routing and train private models on open weights around recurring work. Those models earn production traffic by meeting the same bar as the APIs they replace.

Over time, frontier APIs handle only the tasks that still require them. The rest runs on models the company owns, on infrastructure it controls, inside the applications where the work happens.
one_liner: Earned Intelligence for every company.

name: Bizmark
long_description:
Bizmark is the operating system for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods.

Legacy ERPs force operators into templates that don’t reflect how the business runs. As a result, decisions that directly affect revenue, margins, and service levels are made from spreadsheets, with less information than the company has, often by whoever is closest, not whoever knows best.

Bizmark solves this by connecting to the systems, inboxes, spreadsheets, documents, and the knowledge that lives in people’s heads, then turning that context into optimized decisions and automated workflows. Bizmark adapts to how each company operates, not the other way around. And customers get a working product in weeks, not years.

Some of the most innovative American companies use Bizmark to transform their operations.
one_liner: The OS for companies that make, move, or sell physical goods

name: Mosaic
long_description:
Mosaic's main product, Ocean, gives people and their coding agents shared memory across every session, so everyone can understand what happened, why decisions were made, and pick up where someone else left off.

We also built Mosaic, a real-time coding environment where multiple people and their agents can work together live. It went viral, defined the multiplayer AI category, and inspired frontier labs like Anthropic.

Together, we’re building the infrastructure for people and agents to share context and work together.
one_liner: Defining the frontier of multiplayer AI.

name: Dialogus
long_description:
Dialogus builds voice agent infrastructure for enterprises.

Most companies can demo an AI voice agent, but getting one into production is hard. Enterprise agents need to connect to phone systems, internal tools, databases, CRMs, messaging channels, human escalation flows, monitoring, and compliance processes.

Dialogus provides the infrastructure to deploy production-grade voice agents that don’t just talk but complete real workflows. Our platform lets enterprises launch agents that collect information, validate it against internal systems, update records, send follow-up messages, and escalate edge cases to humans.
one_liner: Infra for enterprise voice agents.

name: Alloovium
long_description: Alloovium is the document intelligence layer for construction 🏗️ It reads every document and piece of data on a project (contracts, specs, drawings, compliance records, conversations), turning them into answers you can trust and actions with real value: every answer cites its exact source sentence, paperwork is checked clause by clause against the builder's own Integrated Management System, and nothing AI-drafted moves without a human sign-off, with it all compliant by default.
one_liner: Construction paperwork that finally works for your team

name: COACH
long_description:
Coach is the AI sales coach for in-person sales teams.

Reps record every meeting, and our AI figures out what your best closers do differently, then coaches everyone else to do the same, with precise, personalized feedback after every meeting. 

Managers finally see 100% of what happens in the field: Coach flags who's stuck and why, so they only step in when it matters, and can coach 5× more reps.

And every meeting feeds one sales brain, so leadership finally gets answers to the questions that used to be guesswork. They finally see the game of their team not just the scoreboard.

Our bet: in the AI era, in-person sales will only matter more. It may end up being one of the last truly human jobs.

Our conviction: any motivated rep can become a great one, meeting after meeting.

The results so far: +32% average lift in conversion rate.

COΛCH, post-game video analysis for field sales reps. YC S26
one_liner: The AI Coach for in person sales reps.

name: Audun
long_description: Audun automates debt collection.
one_liner: AI-native debt collection

name: Marble
long_description:
Marble is the first AI-native operating system for the restaurant back-of-house. 

Restaurants, cafes and bars still run on a patchwork of disconnected point solutions, spreadsheets, clipboards and tribal knowledge, which costs the industry billions each year in stockouts, food waste, and lost profit. 

Marble replaces that entire stack with one system. Computer vision and voice AI capture real-time inventory levels 90% faster than manual counts, ML models forecast item-level demand at 97% accuracy, and AI agents run dozens of end-to-end workflows autonomously, from procurement and invoice reconciliation to scheduling, food prep, menu engineering, and more.
one_liner: The autonomous back-of-house for restaurants.

name: Stoa
long_description: Stoa provides pricing and trading infrastructure for AI hardware, live with an RFQ marketplace where companies buy and sell GPUs through vetted dealers real-time.
one_liner: The market behind AI hardware.

name: Glen
long_description:
Glen is unified context for every agent and human on your team. Most MCP tools hand an agent a slice, one Slack thread, a single diff, and leave it to stitch the rest together itself. Glen reads from where your work already lives, code and PRs, issues, docs, and meetings, reconciles it, and gives your agents the full picture instead.

With Glen a coding agent knows why a line was written, not just what it says. Ask a PR assistant anything about a change and the clarifying-question relay disappears. Bug bots read the intent behind the code before they comment, so they stop flagging deliberate choices as defects and stop repeating mistakes they already made. A sales agent can coach your head of sales off the full account history, how teammates handle similar calls, what was promised, where the deal stalled, etc. 

As the work gets done, Glen also distills it into skills and offers them back to the next agent, or person, who hits the same task.
one_liner: Unified organizational context for agents and humans

name: Context.dev
long_description:
Context.dev gives AI agents structured data from any website through a single API.

We help developers build smarter agents & products that depend on accurate, fresh web data.

If you need structured data from the internet, you need Context.dev

Proud to power agentic products at Mintlify, Super, Vizzy, Klarna, and 400+ other companies.
one_liner: We give AI agents realtime web context.

name: Codag
one_liner: Log compression for agents.

name: Exosat
long_description:
Exosat is building thousands of low-cost communication satellites to provide a neutral, sovereign alternative to Starlink. By building our satellites with zero ITAR/EAR-controlled content, we can leverage manufacturers anywhere in the world to produce our satellites at under a tenth of the cost and launch them from any nation to bypass launch capacity bottlenecks.

We're starting off by selling connectivity to device OEMs and network operators, but will eventually use the distributed compute across our constellation to run low-latency inference for robots and autonomous vehicles in remote and rural areas anywhere on the planet.

We've already signed $400M+ in LOIs to work with operators across Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, booked our first satellite launch next year, and hold an 11,000 satellite filing with the ITU to build the largest comms network outside of the U.S. and China.
one_liner: Building a sovereign Starlink

name: Touchmark
long_description: Buy tokens over a time window from the provider of your choice at a price fixed today - 10-30% off the on-demand price. If your plans change - resell your reserved capacity to another buyer.
one_liner: Market for future inference capacity

name: Prodigy Research
long_description: Prodigy is the frontier AI trading research lab. We've trained the world's best foundation model for quantitative finance. We've already achieved more than 100% returns in live trading over the course of our YC batch, doubling our capital while major indices were flat. Our founders previously built strategies that generated billions in trading profits at Jane Street, trained frontier AI models at Google DeepMind and shipped cutting-edge AI at Apple to billions of customers. Join us as we use AI to solve the market.
one_liner: Training the world's best foundation model for quantitative finance.

name: Zaplar
long_description:
Zaplar is the AI-native operating system for hotels.

Hotels run on legacy software and a fragmented tech stack. Zaplar replaces the entire hotel tech stack (PMS, POS, booking engine, etc) into one software that can handle hotel operations autonomously.

Learn more at https://zaplar.com
one_liner: Agentic Hotel Operating System

name: screenpipe
long_description: screenpipe record and learns how you work and turns it into a searchable memory, documents, and AI agents. Data is stored on your device or where your team choose, open source.
one_liner: AI powered by everything you've seen, said or heard

name: Manifold
long_description:
The US Warehouse industry spends $75bn on labor each year. Yet, only 10% of US warehouses have any form of automation, because existing robotics are too expensive and hard to integrate. 

Manifold deploys autonomous robots that handle picking, loading / unloading, and palletizing — priced by pick. Integration in hours. No upfront costs. No retrofitting. No need to rebuild the operation around the robot. 

Our mission is to make it easy for any warehouse to adopt robotics.
one_liner: Low-cost, deployment-ready robotic labor for warehouses

name: Rasyn
one_liner: Towards a General Intelligence for Chemistry

name: Alkera AI
long_description: Alkera is a data engineering/analysis/science agent that works in your IDE or CLI. If you’re tired of agents that produce false, or even dangerous, reports about your data, then Alkera is for you. Our agent is equipped with your data’s history and lineage, your team’s knowledge, and tailored plugins for data apps such as Snowflake and dbt. Simply install and connect your services to begin doing trusted agentic data work. We also offer VPC & on-prem deployment options for when data can't leave your boundary.
one_liner: Reliable and safe data engineering and data science agents

name: Definite
long_description:
Definite is where finance teams build everyday back-office agents on one live model of their books. We plug into your ERP, ledger, payroll, and payments read-only and compile everything into one clean model that stays current as money moves. Your back-office team then builds agents on top in plain English. We never write back and we never move money. The agents are yours, the plumbing is ours.

We met in first year computer science at Waterloo and interned at Meta, Optiver, and BitGo. At Optiver they ran an n8n hackathon and the interns automated basically nothing. It couldn't talk to the systems that mattered. When we pitched banks and fintechs on agents, they kept telling us the same thing. The agent isn't the hard part, getting clean data out of their systems is.

Right now, automating anything in a back office means engineers hand-stitching data from a dozen sources in different formats on different schedules. Tools like n8n and Workato assume your data is already clean and joined. In finance it never is. So the teams with the most repetitive work and smallest budgets get nothing.

The hard part is the compiler. Every source gets cleaned, matched, and joined into one live model of transactions, invoices, vendors, and payments, and it has to stay right as money lands every day. 

Everyone throws engineers at this. We're doing it once so nobody has to again. Every back office is getting agents eventually. Whoever owns the data they read from owns the thing all of them depend on, and eventually the books themselves. That's what we're building.
one_liner: Build everyday back-office agents on one live model of your books

name: Traceforce
long_description:
AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude have become part of everyone's daily workflow, but they introduce new security risks that traditional security tools weren't built to handle. Security teams at companies from startups to Fortune 500s, are struggling to keep up.

Traceforce gives a company’s security team visibility of how AI apps are being used across company’s devices, and the ability to detect and prevent security breaches and unsafe actions as early as possible.
one_liner: Securing AI native apps directly on devices

name: Standard Machines
long_description: We build RL environments to teach AI to design chips.
one_liner: RL Environments For Chip Design

name: Agency Tool Company
long_description:
Agency Tool Company ships software to robots in the field 20x faster than a Docker pull with ATC Deploy, sending only the bytes that changed and resuming when the network drops. Deployment tooling is the connection between the lab & the field that continually bottlenecks robotics scaling and lacks a strong robotics-native solution. Deploy is live today with 3 launch partners across ag, construction, and logistics robotics.

Our second product, ATC Build, offers embedded-compute as a CI service so devs can run tests and validate their software on the actual target hardware. Build supports the Nvidia Jetson lineup, Raspberry Pi, and a number of other embedded platform targets.

Jack Morrison and Davis Foster founded and sold Scythe Robotics after deploying hundreds of autonomous mowers across the country; Agency Tool Company is building the robotics deployment platform across hardware and software they wish they had.

Learn more at https://agencytool.com
one_liner: Reliable infrastructure to build, deploy and manage real-world robots.

name: Cerenovus
long_description:
Cerenovus is a company brain. We aggregate every kind of file a company produces — documents, PDFs, emails, Slack messages, spreadsheets, meeting notes — and convert them into a single markdown knowledge graph with native AI-agent integration. A company's information becomes uniformly readable both by humans and by the AI agents working inside the graph.

On top of that foundation, Cerenovus maps the company as a system, drawing connections between the people, processes, and tools that make up real workflows. From that systems map, it infers where operations are inefficient and how to improve them.

In practice, this tool will help executives make better decisions. Whenever a leader has to act on a question — how to restructure a team, whether to keep a vendor, or where handoffs between teams are breaking down — Cerenovus will give them an evidence-backed answer in minutes rather than weeks.

Today, that work is done by consultants, by internal analysts, or by the executive asking around informally. Each of those approaches is slow, partial, and goes stale the moment it is delivered. Cerenovus produces the same answers faster, at a fraction of the cost, and keeps them live as the company evolves.
one_liner: A knowledge company

name: Molagri
long_description:
Molagri develops safer, more effective pesticides for agriculture.

We design biopesticides that hit a precise molecular target unique to pest insects, knocking out pests while sparing pollinators, beneficial insects, and the wider ecosystem. By modeling how pests are likely to evolve, we stay a step ahead of resistance, keeping our products effective against the pests of today and tomorrow. The higher efficacy and biobased production will also contribute to emissions reductions in both manufacturing and field use.

Our founders are PhD lab mates from the University of Toronto who have worked together for six years and published in Nature Communications and Nature Microbiology.
one_liner: Resistance free pesticides.

name: Stratum Industries
long_description:
Stratum builds AI agents that clear the U.S. government backlog. Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, and benefits claim in America has to be reviewed by a government adjudicator and the software they rely on was built decades before AI. The result is millions of applications stuck in queues: veterans waiting on disability ratings, families waiting on pensions, builders waiting years to break ground.

Stratum replaces that workflow. A reviewer drops in an application, selects the rubric it needs to be checked against, and an agent plans, executes, and reviews the file end to end routing each step to the right model for the most accurate and cost-efficient decision. Hundreds of agents run in parallel in the cloud, with a human kept in the loop to approve and full auditability at every step, so an entire backlog can be cleared in the time it used to take to review a single file.

We're rebuilding the entire infrastructure the government runs on both the reviewer side and the applicant side - so filing and adjudication become instant instead of taking weeks.

We're Vihaan and Raj, brothers. Vihaan was founding engineer #3 at Cadastral (acquired by Legora) and dropped out of Waterloo to build Stratum. Raj led GTM at Deel, averaging 220% of quota over two years and ranking top 5 of 1,000+ reps globally, and dropped out of grad school at the University of Bath to build Stratum.
one_liner: AI agents that clear the U.S. government backlog.

name: FlowManual
long_description:
FlowManual is the all-in-one AI bidding and purchasing platform for both general and MEP construction contractors.

Built by two engineers and Harvard dropouts, FlowManual automates the buying process during pre-construction. With FlowManual, specialty contractors win more work while general contractors deliver at higher standards.
one_liner: AI for Construction's Back Office.

name: Pluto
long_description:
Resumes made careers readable. LinkedIn made them searchable. Pluto makes them understood.

Professionals talk to Pluto for 10 minutes about what they’ve done, what they’re great at, and what they want next. Pluto makes that context discoverable to the right people and AI agents, helping them understand the professional more fully.

For hiring, companies tell Pluto who they want to meet. Pluto searches its network and the broader market, evaluates fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and makes warm introductions when both sides want to connect.

18K+ professionals have shared their career context with Pluto. 100+ companies, from fast-growing startups to decacorns, use Pluto to meet people with deeper context and confirmed interest.
one_liner: AI voice agent that helps professionals get discovered

name: machine0
long_description:
machine0 is a CLI for agent compute: `machine0 new mybox` gives your agent a full cloud VM, billed by the minute, from small up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB and 8×H100s. Agents drive it themselves via CLI or MCP.

Agent workloads are moving from ephemeral to always-on. A coding agent working on a hard feature runs 6-8 hours. Auto-research agents run for days. machine0 is the environment in which these agents run.
one_liner: Cloud computers for AI agents

name: Bloomy
long_description: Bloomy helps students learn more efficiently by using AI to identify exactly what a student should learn and when they should learn it. We provide adaptive and personalized curriculum to K-12, starting with English Language Arts, Math, and Writing.
one_liner: AI-powered mastery learning for K-12

name: 6thSense
one_liner: A nervous system for physical AI

name: Nori
long_description:
Nori builds home robots that cost less than $2,000 and that anyone can teach. Out of the box, the NORI L3 does household chores: loading the dishwasher, folding laundry, tidying up. But because anyone can train it, it also learns your specific tasks, like washing paintbrushes if you're an artist or flipping sheet music while you play guitar. It's a general-purpose robot, not an appliance.

We launched pre-orders 6 weeks ago and have already booked $100K in revenue.

Humanoid robots exist, but they cost $20,000 or more and are demoed, not shipped. We got to $1,688 without sacrificing capability. Instead of expensive actuators, we use low-cost servos and get more out of them through smarter control and design. A wheeled base with a lift gives full floor-to-counter reach without the cost and fragility of legs, and we streamlined manufacturing from day one, assembling in the US.

The teachability is the moat. Every skill a user trains can be shared, so each customer makes every robot more capable. Hardware is the entry point; the skill ecosystem is the recurring revenue.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia labs like RoboPIL (robot learning) and CGUI. Working with $100K research robots that struggled with everyday tasks convinced us the problem isn't capability, it's cost. Good robots don't need to be expensive.

Households already spend $2,000+ on single-task machines: a dishwasher, a washing machine, a vacuum. We sell one robot at $1,688 that does the work of all of them and learns more. At 5% of US households and $25 a month for skills, that's $2B a year in recurring revenue, on top of hardware.
one_liner: Affordable robot you can teach to do anything

name: Ooak Data
long_description:
The promise of AI agents is still unmet in complex, real-world business environments. Our mission is to make it possible for agents to reliably accomplish concrete and useful tasks.

That’s why we're building **Alexandria,** the world's largest library of real-world business workflow datasets.
one_liner: We build the world's largest library of real-world business workflow…

name: Graphify Labs
long_description:
Graphify builds queryable knowledge graphs from local codebases, docs, and Jira (105K+ GitHub stars, ~4.2M downloads, used in production by engineers at Rootly, Geotab, Tweddle Group, and Superagent). 

On that graph, its enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change, proving the new behavior matches the old or handing back the exact input that breaks it. The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current graph of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads. 

Runs fully on-premise, so no data leaves the building.
one_liner: On-device knowledge graph engine for enterprises

name: Greypoint Industries
long_description: Greypoint Industries built LEGION, a drone swarm that identifies, geolocates, and tracks every emitter on the battlefield using the enemy’s own radio signals. LEGION enables our warfighters to precisely track previously obscured targets like jammers, command posts, and drone operators so they can proactively respond to threats instead of reacting to them.
one_liner: Manufacturing the future of autonomous swarm warfare.

name: TareBio
long_description: Our platform develops personalized or population-level vaccines for any disease in weeks by changing only one input: the immune imprint. Instead of trying to predict which antigens might work, we read out immune cells already fighting the disease in the body and reverse-engineer antigens that activate them. We've already run our platform end-to-end and created a vaccine that cured cancer in mice.
one_liner: Vaccines for any cancer or infection in weeks.

name: Almanac
long_description: Almanac is Hermes with a company brain. You message it in Slack or iMessage; it knows what is happening across your company and can use your accounts to get real tasks done for you. It has a full computer, browser and terminal. It takes your Gmail, Calendar, Attio, GitHub, AI convos, docs and meeting notes and compiles them into a Wiki that keeps itself up to date. It keeps a current understanding of what you’re building, who your customers are, what was decided, and what still needs to happen. It can use websites, run code, create files and take actions across your accounts. If it reaches a login, payment or decision it shouldn’t make alone, it pings you or hands you the live browser.
one_liner: The AI that knows your company

name: Orvixo
long_description: Orvixo uses AI to build reactive end-to-end planning and optimisation models for manufacturers.
one_liner: AI advanced planning and optimisation for manufacturers.

name: Whitespace
long_description: Whitespace is the AI operating system for wholesale distributors. It connects to their systems and inboxes to build a living model of their business, then deploys self-improving AI agents to automate work like inventory planning, customer support, and order entry.
one_liner: AI Operating System for Wholesale Distributors

name: Click
long_description:
Click builds chat-native work services for ChatGPT and Claude. 
We’re starting with a research service that brings live external context from professional & social platforms, financial markets, maps, travel sources - and a lot more - into the conversation. 
It makes research on people & companies even deeper with specialized, source-backed context beyond built-in web search, while enabling new tasks like comparing live flight fares right inside the chat.
one_liner: Web search & connectors for agents

name: Vendo
long_description:
Vendo is the customization layer that lets your users build their own features and micro-apps directly on top of your product. Rather than waiting on an ever-growing feature backlog, your users can personalize the product to exactly how they work, create their own automations, and integrate hundreds of external tools, all without your team writing a line of code.

Everything runs on your existing API, renders natively in your own theme and components, and executes inside secure sandboxes within your existing security guardrails, so your source code is never touched. Companies can plug Vendo into an agent they already have, or deploy a production-ready agent complete with the ability to take actions in the product, generate UI, and draw on a built-in knowledge base. Vendo is open source and installs with a single command, and we work closely with teams to get it running for their product.
one_liner: Let your users build their own features on top of your product

name: Aktoria Robotics
long_description: Operate any robot, anywhere in the world.
one_liner: Human as API for robots

name: Rational
long_description: Rational builds AI coworkers for accounting firms. Our agents onboard themselves to the firm, build a company brain, and do the work, from month-end close to tax prep. In addition, they follow up with clients and communicate with the right members of your team.
one_liner: AI Employees for Accounting

name: Omanta
long_description:
Omanta is a personalized research lab for patients who have exhausted standard options, want to prepare proactively for recurrence, or are living with an unresolved diagnosis.

We direct the full operational infrastructure, personnel, expertise, and technology of a large research program toward understanding and addressing the challenges of individual patients across oncology, rare disease, and undiagnosed conditions.

For clinicians, we act as a collaborative partner, providing a living roadmap for ongoing patient care built on a rigorous and evolving scientific evidence base.

We fully operationalize patient-specific research programs, covering tissue logistics, diagnostic follow-up, data integration, multiomic analysis, therapeutic strategy development, and more.

Omanta brings context and clarity to complex cases, helping clinicians see more of the scientific picture as they decide how best to care for their patients.
one_liner: A research lab for one

name: Fabraix
long_description:
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. On AgentHarm, the leading benchmark for offensive AI security, Nyx achieved a 78% attack success rate, compared with 67% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions.

Nyx often finds its first vulnerability within minutes or hours rather than days or weeks. Because the work is fully automated, companies can repeat the test with every change and at a much lower cost than what a 7-figure red-teaming (and point-in-time) engagement would require.

We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.
one_liner: The world's frontier hacker for AI agents.

name: Qlo
long_description: Qlo uses AI to automate commercial underwriting end to end, from submission through renewal, for MGAs and program administrators.
one_liner: AI that automates underwriting for commercial insurance carriers

name: Daqstra
long_description: Daqstra is the AI-native orchestration layer for physical R&D. It saves engineers in Aerospace, Energy and Robotics hundreds of man hours managing test infrastructure by connecting fragmented test hardware, bringing live and historical test data into one place, and by giving engineers an API to orchestrate their entire test setup. We enable teams to spend less time rebuilding test infrastructure and more time improving the hardware they test.
one_liner: AI-native orchestration for physical R&D testing

name: Risklytics
long_description: Risklytics is a commercial insurance brokerage for frontier tech: robotics, autonomy, data centers, and energy infrastructure. Insurers are writing AI exclusions into standard liability forms, so companies whose products act in the physical world end up holding risk they thought they had transferred. We specialize in that gap, and we know which carriers in the admitted and surplus lines markets will still underwrite it. If you're building anything that moves, lifts, drives, or powers something, we'd like to talk.
one_liner: Commercial Insurance Brokerage for Frontier Tech

name: LATO
long_description:
The best investments come from conviction, and conviction comes from understanding a market deeply: its customers, its competitors, and where it's heading.

Today that understanding is slow and expensive to build. Reaching the right people takes weeks, a commercial study costs $300k+, and each one starts from scratch.

LATO does this research end-to-end, combining public data and the fund's own knowledge with first-hand interviews of a market's customers, experts, and operators. This research grounds a simulation of the market to predict how market participants behave.

On PokerClubhub, players deposit with PokerClubHub, not the club owner. We handle all deposits and withdrawals for the club owner, saving them time and increasing their earnings. We pay the rake (if any) to club owners as affiliate fees.

After that, every run is watched - IT is alerted the moment something fails, agents nobody uses get retired. long_description:

long_description:
hiloop helps teams train agents for tasks where general models are not good enough. Reach out to us for early access at founders@hiloop.ai.

name: Robocurve
long_description:
Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust.

Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits.

Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once.

Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.
one_liner: Evaluating robots in the real world.

name: Salem Robotics Inc
long_description: Our software turns any robot we deploy into an everyday independent worker at your facility. They are able to walk sites, handle instruments, overcome obstacles, collect measurements, and generate auditable compliance records, replacing hours of mandatory manual surveys and inspections. Built by Los Alamos robotics veterans and deterministic-manipulation researchers, we're starting in nuclear and expanding to other hazardous industries.

name: Osseus
long_description:
Osseus is the intelligent development platform for robotics. It plugs into the tools a team already uses - CAD, ECAD, GitHub, Jira, docs, messaging, and test runs - creating a live dependency graph of their entire robot stack. It automatically builds and maintains the relationships between every part, board, requirement, test, and decision.

When a hardware change is made, the map traces the downstream impact across mechanical, electrical, and software. Osseus's agents find which requirements may be compromised, run the attached tests and sims, create fixes for the affected hardware/software on branches, and re-run the tests to confirm the new design doesn’t break downstream.

Osseus includes a robotics component marketplace. Teams can list spare parts and hardware for others to buy/rent during prototyping, and designs can be evaluated against real component availability. If a part has a long lead time or is unavailable, engineers can quickly find compatible alternatives in their area instead of waiting weeks or asking around their network.

Design review also happens in Osseus. Engineers see why a design might not work, what's been tried before, and why something was built the way it was, pulled from prior conversations between engineers and with suppliers. Suppliers comment directly on a part through a secure link instead of back and forth over email, and what they say is remembered. If a supplier flags that a design isn't machinable, or that changing a feature would cut cost, that insight automatically appears the next time someone designs something similar, saving time and money.

We ultimately will use the platform's deep engineering understanding to develop physical-AI models that reason jointly over the robot's geometry, electronics, kinematics, components, software, and real-world performance so people can optimize and iterate on robots much faster. name: Caution
all_locations: George Town, George Town, Cayman Islands
long_description:
Caution is a hosting platform for software you can't afford to get hacked. It simplifies and extends confidential compute, and lets developers deploy workloads to secure enclaves in minutes and give customers, auditors, and counterparties cryptographic proof that production is running the exact reviewed source code, build, configuration, and runtime - not an opaque binary controlled by a cloud operator or internal admin.

Confidential computing hardware exists, but the tooling is too fragmented and incomplete for most teams to use well. Today, attestation often proves only that a binary has a certain hash; it does not prove what source code produced that binary. Building the missing deployment, reproducibility, and verification layer requires specialized security engineering and often locks teams into one cloud or hardware stack. Caution turns that into a simple git-based workflow that builds reproducible enclave images, provisions infrastructure, and lets anyone independently verify what is running.

We built Caution after years securing high-risk systems through Distrust, where we worked with hedge funds, custodians, blockchain teams, cloud platforms, and critical grid operators on systems responsible for more than $600B in assets. Again and again, the same problem showed up: teams running mission-critical infrastructure could not reliably prove what was executing in production.

As AI, fintech, healthcare, and regulated data collaboration move into the cloud, "trust us" is no longer enough. Caution is a general-purpose platform: if it runs on a server, it can run verifiably on Caution. We're starting where trust failures cost the most, but we believe verifiable compute will become the default way software runs, the same way HTTPS became the default way it's served. Infrastructure you can verify, not trust.
one_liner: Hosting platform for software you don't want to get hacked

name: Coasty
long_description:
Coasty is a computer use agent that does real work inside softwares, companies already run. New web apps, old desktop tools, the legacy systems nobody wants to touch. You hand it a workflow and it owns the outcome.
Most agents demo well and break the moment they hit real software. They get 18 steps out of 20 right, misclick once, and everything after is garbage. Coasty catches when it goes off track and fixes itself mid-task instead of starting over. It handles the messy parts, benchmarks never show. Permission dialogs, surprise pop-ups, a modal that steals focus, a page that loads slow. When a vendor pushes an overnight update and moves half the menus, brittle scripts break by morning. Coasty reads the screen instead of recording clicks, so it adapts and keeps going.
It also checks its own output and leaves a time-stamped trail you can replay. We won't pretend it gets every task right. Nothing automating this work does. What matters is what happens when something breaks. It catches the mistake, fixes what it can, and flags what it can't so a person can step in. Nothing fails quietly. That's what lets a team trust it on the work where a silent error gets someone fired.
We scored 82% on OSWorld, which puts us among the most reliable agents out there. Reliability is the whole product, not a feature.
one_liner: The computer-use agent that doesn't break on real software. We will…
